their ad in our program.
If you have any questions, please feel free to contact any member at the track, or write
Eastern Wisconsin Stock Cars, Inc., P.O. Box 47, Plymouth, WI 53073.
Thank you and enjoy the evening.

=== COLUMN 1 ===
History of Eastern
Wisconsin Stock Cars
Eastern Wisconsin Stock Cars, Inc. began as a sanctioned body in the year 1960. The
name, however, was discussed and voted on in the May 21, 1959 membership meeting with
it being Eastern Wisconsin Stock Car Association. Prior to 1960 Erwald Stock of Manitowoc
was the promoter. The actual inception of Eastern Wisconsin Stock Cars as a sanctioning
body started at the March, 7, 1960 membership meeting when the VFW wanted the Associa-
tion to co-promote the races at the Fairgrounds. At the next meeting, however, the VFW
decided not to take part in the promoting. Bob Akright and Gene Bonnett then said they
would promote the races if the Association could loan them $400 to get things started. At
the May meeting the club accepted Bob Akright and Harold Laack as the promoters. Gate
admission in 1960 was adults $1.00, 8-14 was $ .50, and under 8 free. Pit passes were $1.50.
In July of 1960 the club decided to divide up the money in the treasury at the end of the
season and give it to the drivers. Only enough money was kept in the treasury to start the
races the following season. Officers of the first EWSCA were Lanny Schirmer - President,
Bob Akright - Vice President, and Kermit Schulz was elected Secretary - Treasurer. In
September of that year the club established a policy that would require cars to race at half
of the races or no point bonus. Also in that meeting the Chilton Fair Board asked if the
club would race there once a month if they built a quarter-mile track, and the club agreed.
EWSCA previously raced on the half mile. The first point payoff was held October 29, 1960
at the Oak Park Tavern.
Starting in 1961, the Association decided to run the Chilton track on Wednesday nights.
A car had to complete at least half the races at each track to qualify for the point payoff.
1961 officers were President - Harry Wiessgerber, Vice President - Terry Fee, and Secretary
Kermit Schulz. Bob Akright and Happy Laack were voted as track managers for both tracks.
Four directors were added to the Board in 1961, the four being Harvey Miller, Marvin
Halschback, Andy Levchenko, and Bill Fitzgerald. In September the club prohibited women
from being in the pits and from being members. (These rulings have since been changed).
Spectator cars got their start during the 1961 racing season with no points awarded. Prizes
such as a jacket, oil, patches, or other merchandise were given. Point payoff party in 1961
was held at Andy's Place on October 28.
Board of directors in 1962 consisted of President Harry Wiessgerber, Vice President Don
Diener, Secretary Bernard Dineen, Treasurer Eldo Zander, and Board members Andy Lev-
chenko, Harvey Kuester, and Harvey Miller.
Sportsman rules were also being formed as the spectator class was getting out of hand,
since they had few rules. The sportsman class was officially started in 1963 with the rules
committee consisting of Russ Waldron, Jim Weisner, Frank Kraus, Bob Akright, and Happy
Laack. Some of the early stars in the sportman division included Oscar Konen, Milt Schaef-
fer, Buck Carmen, Richard Hed, Russ Waldron, LeRoy Dickmann, Ken Steffen and Paul
Ziegelbauer. Modified stars included Ken Markwardt, Carl Kuhlow, Lanny Schirmer, Don
Diener, Woody Klug, Ken Painter, Tom Sippel, and Bill Eickberg, just to name a few.
In 1967 the 1/4 oval at Plymouth was lengthened slightly and had new clay added. Hobby
Stocks were added to the program in 1970. During the first year the drivers ran for trophies
and in 1971 were under the point system.
In 1972 EWSCA received a shot in the arm as many of the Milwaukee Stock Car Racing
Association started competing at the Plymouth and Chilton tracks. Two years later the club
ended its twelve year competition at the Chilton tracks. Special shows were run at the
Calumet County fairgrounds in Chilton, the most noted is the appearance of EWSCA at the
fair.
In 1968, the club made weekly appearances at 141 Speedway in Francis Creek. EWSCA
sanctioned races there for six years on Thursday nights and later Wednesday nights. With
dwindling fields of cars and added expenses the club stopped running in 1982 after member-
ship approval.
Before the 1984 racing season the track at Plymouth was moved fifty feet to the east and
was lengthened from a quarter mile to one-third mile. In 1985 a large metal grandstand was
constructed which seated 4036 people. Besides Plymouth and Chilton, Eastern Wisconsin
Stock Cars has sanctioned races at Beaver Dam and Fond du Lac.
Membership has grown steadily through the years, from less than 100 in 1960 to over
1100 in 1989. Over 100 drivers compete weekly in the three divisions: modifieds, sportsman,
and hobby stock.

=== COLUMN 1 ===
Alky - alcohol, used as racing fuel.
Banking - inclination of the race track usually on the corners.
Bite - traction of wheels on racetrack.
Black Flag - signal used by officials to call a driver into pits for consultation,
usually to check suspected damage to car or for disciplinary reason.
Blend - racing fuel mixture, usually composed of methanol and nitromethane.
Block - cylinder block of an internal combustion engine.
Blower - supercharger.
Blown Engine - (1) a supercharged engine; (2) an engine that has failed.
Bore - measurement across the diameter of a cylinder.
Brake Fade - brake effectiveness lost because of overheating.
Brake Line - hydraulic brake hose connecting master cylinder with wheel cylinder.
Broke - eliminated from competition by mechanical failure.
Bubble - position in which a car is in the most imminent danger of being
bumped" from the starting lineup by a faster qualifier; i.e. - "He is on the bubble."
Bullring - an oval track of a half-mile or less.
Cam - eccentric formation on a shaft to transform a rotating motion into
reciprocating.
Camber - angle at which the wheels sit on the track.
Camshaft - shaft which operates valves or valve actuating mechanisms in
internal combustion engines.
Caster - inclination to the rear of the top of the front axle.
Chassis - basic frame of a car without running gear.
Cheat - violate rules of competition.
Checkered Flag - flag of black and white squares that indicates finish of race.
Chief Steward - top official of a race.
Chop - (1) to cut off another car in a corner; (2) to alter a chassis.
Chute - a straightaway.
C.I.D. - cubic inch displacement.
Coils; Coil Springs - members of the suspension system.
Compound - mixture of various components in tire-building.
Compression Ratio - ratio of uncompressed to compressed volume in an
engine cylinder bore.
Con Rod - connecting rod which ties together piston and crankshaft in an
internal combustion engine.
Crankcase - pan or sump on underside of engine to hold oil.
Crankshaft - shaft driven by the action of the pistons, which transmits power to
the drive train.
Decal - transfer sheets used on race cars to promote various companies.
Differential - gear-driven rear axle assembly that transmits power from drive
shaft to rear wheels.
Disks - round steel surfaces onto which brake pads clamp when brakes are
applied.
Displacement - volume in cubic measure of cylinder or engine; it can be
expressed in either cubic inches or cubic centimeters.
DOHC - double overhead camshaft.
Drafting - following closely behind another car to take advantage of the resulting
decreased wind resistance and vacuum effect, thus cutting down on fuel
consumption; also known as slipstreaming.
Drift - controlled four-wheel slide, a technique used in cornering.
